profile.headline: at Vizdom Software, Inc
profile.geoLocationName: San Luis Obispo, California, United States
profile.summary:
Summary of Qualifications:

Twenty-five years of solid commercial software engineering experience in various positions of heightened responsibilities in enhancing existing technologies; and embracing, pioneering and designing new technologies to develop easily maintainable complete solutions.  

Sound problem solving and design skills yield modular solutions with clean interfaces suitable for object-oriented, parallel, and distributed designs.  Possess excellent abstraction and spatial relations skills, which enhance my ability to visualize the flow and interactions of entire systems.

Strong grasp of programming concepts considered "difficult," such as concurrency through multi-processing, multi-tasking, and multi-threading, recursion, object-oriented design, and distributed computation.

Have implemented and maintained highly portable software.
Used many different communication mechanisms to build modular, parallel, clustered, and distributed systems.

Implemented operating system level constructs such as preemptive thread schedulers, message passing mechanisms, cache management, virtual memory management, inter-process communication, lexical analysis, dynamic binding, real-time control, and device drivers.

Developed products in many diverse fields, including system software, utilities, compilers, operating systems, network communications, embedded software, machine control, robotics, Internet and Web based applications, end user productivity applications, scientific applications, graphic image manipulation, streaming media, and knowledge management systems.

Write clearly, communicating ideas effectively over a wide spectrum of technical needs, from design specifications and object documentation to end user manuals.  Delivered countless technology talks including training for internal and external engineers, customer pre- and post-sales presentations, company-wide briefings, and conference presentations.

Specialties: Object-Oriented Analysis and Design, Software Systems Architecture, Software Design Review and Consultation.  Software development for Mac OS X, Linux, and Unix systems.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: Vizdom provides system design and development services to major corporations, with a focus on Document Management and Enterprise Content Management systems. Recent projects provide access to content in proprietary document stores for an enterprise search product. Most components consist of web services constructed using Java and Spring and embedded databases, and deployed in Tomcat.

positions.title: Independent Software Contractor
positions.description: After moving to the California central coast, I engaged in several small software development contracts with local clients, as well as clients in the S.F. Bay Area, the L.A. area and even the east coast.  Among these projects were: enterprise search product analysis, design and deployment; environmental noise analysis and modeling; Virtual Team Collaboration technology; a scalable enterprise network file system; mobile directional antennae aiming and telemetry; presentation software; and learning software for those with speech disabilities.  The projects ranged from embedded software, desktop applications, and server-side services.  Implementation languages were typically Java, C dialects, and scripting languages.

positions.title: Principal Software Architect
positions.description: Re-architected many key components of the core retrieval technology: "objectifying" them for easier maintainability, extensibility, and performance.  Modifications provided thousand-fold increases in performance across the board.   Co-designer and implementer of a parallel, distributed search server for Internet and Enterprise deployment.  Laid out a component strategy that allowed the concurrent development and integration of Verity's suite of products.  Redesigned the entire document access abstraction to enable increased concurrency, better metadata access, and support for automated exploration and indexing (spiders) over a wide variety of document repositories.   Instrumental in the design and implementation of Verity's core full text search technology.  Designed and implemented a network transparent message passing, multi-threaded infrastructure portable to many platforms.  I acted as the technical lead of the team building Verity's real time document classification engine.

positions.title: Software contractor
positions.description: Developed software for a silicon wafer cooling station and a wafer-handling robot for a high-vacuum silicon wafer processing system.  An object-oriented ANSI-C framework was used for implementation of the control software, which was cross-compiled to an embedded Motorola 68000-based control computer.  Extensive design and implementation documentation was delivered for third-party integration.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
1989 - 1993  Contract Software Engineer.  Developed a NeXT workstation to IBM mainframe connectivity package.  As the principal software engineer for this project, was solely responsible for the overall architectural design, GUI design using Interface Builder, object-oriented programming using Objective-C, distributed client/server computing using Mach messaging, device independent connection drivers, and firmware design.

1983 -1985	Senior Software Engineer. Instrumental in the implementation of an MS-DOS operating system and utilities for microcomputers designed for distributed systems.  Then developed an IBM PC to IBM mainframe connectivity package which involved inter-process communication via remote procedure calls, overlay management, device independent connection drivers, and a multi-threaded print spooler.

positions.title: Software contractor
positions.description: As primary software developer for the Lotus Manuscript Technical Word Processing system through its first two releases, implemented a process manager, virtual memory manager, dynamic linking loader, dyna-link library, menu system, utilities, and many performance enhancements. Solely responsible for porting the system from MS-DOS to OS/2.
